newsitem.title: INDIA: India FICCI seeks steps to bolster small investors.
newsitem.headline: India FICCI seeks steps to bolster small investors.

text.p: One of India's leading industry associations has asked the government to take steps to bring back small investors scared away by last year's declines on the country's stock exchanges.

In a memorandum to Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, faxed to Reuters on Monday, the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) asked the government to permit forward contracts and abolish limits on bank lending against shares.

The memorandum, submitted ahead of the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) scheduled to be presented next month, asked Chidambaram to extend to companies a facility to buy back their shares from the market, a FICCI statement said.
"It is imperative to give a clear signal to small investors to return to the capital market actively," the statement said.
"Capital market has been deserted by the small and retail investors...," the statement said.
"The investment institutions are illiquid and the capital market is singly looking to the FIIs (foreign institutional investors) for investments which has created instability," it added.
FICCI also urged the government to abolish a minimum alternate tax (MAT) on companies without introducing any compensating tax.
MAT was imposed last year on companies that earlier evaded tax by using a legal loophole that offered tax exemptions on profits ploughed back into business.

The MAT is cited as a major reason for a fall in share prices. The sensitive index (Sensex) of the country's premier Bombay stock exchange, which was at a high of 4,131.22 last year, slumped as low as 2,713.12 after the tax was introduced.
